{{Short description|Japanese mathematician (1930–1995)}}
{{Nihongo|'''Hideyuki Matsumura'''|松村 英之||1930–1995}} was a Japanese [[mathematician]] particularly known for his textbooks<ref name=Matsumura1>{{cite book |last=Matsumura |first=Hideyuki |author-link=Hideyuki Matsumura |date=1987 |title=Commutative Ring Theory |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/commutative-ring-theory/02819830750568B06C16E6199F3562C1 |location=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9781139171762}}</ref><ref name=Matsumura2>{{cite book |last=Matsumura |first=Hideyuki |author-link=Hideyuki Matsumura |date=1980 |title=Commutative Algebra |location=Reading, Massachusetts |publisher=The Benjamin/Cummings Publishing Company Inc. |isbn=0-8053-7026-9}}</ref> in [[commutative algebra]]. He received his Ph.D. in 1958 from [[Kyoto University]] under the advisory of mathematician [[Yasuo Akizuki]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yasuo Akizuki - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=105069 |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>
